quotes.speaker: Jason Lee
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Lee on the public perception of sexuality and children
quotes.excerpt: I don't think it's too far-fetched to believe that a straight man would prefer that he not have a gay child.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
text_blocks.text: I was curious about your perspective. You seem very level-headed, and some people in that community took such offense to that. You were saying that you understand that a straight man would want a straight son. Why do you think that comes from? Why do you think they are so sensitive?

text_blocks.speaker: Jason Lee
text_blocks.text: People see a clip and that's all they see, and that narrative can run rampant. Obviously, you being a black man in culture and in sports, people may see that and feel a certain way. I didn't see you as being homophobic. The comment that you made was, 'Why would you rather want a thought daughter over a gay son?' when I'm sure you sleep with thoughts. I mean, you slept with Selena Gomez. And then, allegedly, I'm sorry, allegedly. I'm sorry. It's a moment where you made a choice, and I feel like when people are raising their kids, or people have desires to have kids, or have an imagination of what their kid would be or be like, I don't think it's too far-fetched to believe that a straight man would prefer that he not have a gay child. But I'm a gay man who, if I do have a kid, I want that motherfucker to be gay, because our shit is lit.

quotes.speaker: Jason Lee
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Lee on the public's reaction to his sexuality
quotes.excerpt: I don't live in responding to ignorance. I came in as Jason, you came in as who you are.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
text_blocks.text: Do you think that more people now are actually gay, or do you think that they just feel more comfortable coming out because it's normalized in society? I've always had the thought that people are not born that way, and the reason for me thinking that is because, as society accepts it more, there are more people being gay. So that means they weren't born that way, they're becoming that way because it's normalized in society. But you are saying that there are people in the closet that are now feeling more free to express themselves.

text_blocks.speaker: Jason Lee
text_blocks.text: I promise you, I don't know what camera, I don't know what camera, any of you, this camera. Go to your YouTube when this lands. Go read the comments. You're going to see tons of comments before they get to this point that say, 'That's Jason's type, because you are my type.' That's Jason's type, that's Jason's type. Oh, look at what they're talking about. Uh-uh, you have me on the show, he's gay, he's gay, he's gay. They're going to say that. I don't live in responding to ignorance. I came in as Jason, you came in as who you are. We're having a conversation that I think is powerful, but people are always going to digest stuff, especially online, and take what they want from it with their own ignorance or their own fears or their own transgressions or their own confusion and react to it. And so I don't even live in that.

quotes.speaker: Jason Lee
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Lee on the dangers of chasing dreams in Hollywood
quotes.excerpt: you can run into a lot of bad actors here who tell you the pathway to the promised land
quotes.quote: The fakest part of Hollywood is people move here to pursue their dreams and get lost in them. You can run into a lot of bad actors here who tell you the pathway to the promised land of making your dreams come true is changing who you are. When I've proven that you can literally be who you are. Every iteration of me has been a process, and my evolution hasn't been me changing, I've just been growing and evolving. I meet a lot of people who come here and they change because they subscribe to this idea that they have to be something else.

quotes.speaker: Jason Lee
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Lee on the boundaries of doing anything for success
quotes.excerpt: I would do anything to make it, but anything does have boundaries to that and there's limitations
quotes.quote: I would do anything to make it, but anything does have boundaries to that and there's limitations to what anything is. In my opinion, it's not definitive that I would do everything. I'll do anything within reason, I'll do anything within the law, I'll do anything within my moral boundaries, but I'm not going to exceed the limits I've set for myself to achieve a dream that I want because somebody else says they can give it to me.

quotes.speaker: Jason Lee
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Lee on the reality of the Me Too movement
quotes.excerpt: there aren't people here that hold all those cards that say, 'If you do this, you're going to get that.'
quotes.quote: There aren't people here that hold all those cards that say, 'If you do this, you're going to get that.' Yes, the Me Too movement is real and people went through those experiences, but if your moral aptitude is so diminished or so limited that you would do everything to get what you want, then you were set up to fail anyway. Everything you want isn't worth having if it comes at a price of losing yourself.

quotes.quote: Everything Hollywood Unlocked was built on an Instagram, $100 and Love & Hip Hop, and then boom. quotes.quote: You're two black men in the Oscars, like with all the white people in the room, on entertainment's biggest night. The stage that every actor is fighting to be on and that he's been fighting his whole career to win. And on the night you win, you pimp slap Chris Rock. It was unimaginable, but it also is reality that he's a human being. And you know, from people saying cancel Will Smith, cancel Smith, the sad part about that is your whole life you're perfect to everybody's standard and one time you make a mistake, a big mistake, but like it's over for you. The idea of that is insane to me.

quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Lee on being authentically himself

quotes.quote: I've chosen to be someone that whether you agree with me or not, I will speak my mind. I will, I will, you know, not always give the politically correct answer and it comes with its, you know, it is, it is tough, but yeah, I guess that's what guys like us choose. That's actually my next question was, you embrace controversy so much, like how hard has that been for you and how did you even get to the point where you were willing to take that on?

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
text_blocks.text: That's actually my next question was, you embrace controversy so much, like how hard has that been for you and how did you even get to the point where you were willing to take that on?

text_blocks.speaker: Jason Lee
text_blocks.text: I'm sitting here with all types of controversies right now that I'm that I'm juggling, right? Got these plates spinning. I mean, I don't want them, but I embrace it because, you know, I said to some I was speaking it to a group of voters, a group of Democrats the other night and I said, you know, all the stuff that was online about me or whatever that's not true or whatever, that like when you watch your brother get murdered, like when you literally watch your brother, I mean just imagine looking at the family photo you showed me and pick anyone of your brothers who you love and all the memories you've created with them and all the hopes and dreams you all have together and all the future plans and things, and imagine they just get murdered right in front of you. Like that's probably the most painful thing you can experience. Once you've endured that, you just know like everything else is going to be a storm that you'll get through, because you've already weathered you've already weathered a storm that was unimaginable that that the that the strongest person in the world is going to struggle with. So I kind of approach everything with that.

quotes.speaker: Michael Porter Jr.
quotes.summary_phrase: Michael Porter Jr. on overcoming public criticism after his injuries
quotes.excerpt: I saw how fickle people are and how they can rock with you one minute and dump the next.
quotes.quote: That's exactly what turned me into someone that was willing to accept that because I saw how fickle people are and how they can rock with you one minute and dump the next, because I was at the very top at one point in high school. I was the best player. I was projected number one draft pick and then I got injured and I saw the whole basketball world, all these analysts giving their opinion and just tearing me down. Then slowly started being able to play again and people come right back around. I just saw how human nature is. I was hurt by that experience and I've been through a crazy time of my life that now, like you said, some of the little things, people's opinions, they kind of bounce off me. But it's because of going through hardship.

quotes.speaker: Jason Lee
quotes.summary_phrase: Jason Lee on handling public criticism and his political motivations
quotes.excerpt: I take all the criticism that's thrown at me and I literally just like crafted into a crown.
quotes.quote: I take all the criticism that's thrown at me and I literally just like crafted into a crown because you're talking about me. You have an opinion about me. When some of the most powerful people in the world call me for my diss or when some of the most famous people in the world share their vulnerabilities with me, I know who I am and I know that sometimes the narratives I hear about me, he's messy, he's this, he's that. Yeah, some of that's true because I've given you moments to have that opinion. But there's also people who know me here like, yo, if I ever needed somebody to ride or die for me, that's the one I'm calling. I'm the one that people have called to walk them through some of the most complicated stuff and I find myself going through the fire sometimes and I just always say to God, I know you're putting me through this for a reason. I went home, got elected in the city that I grew up in that almost killed me. I went back to change things for kids and for the community and I've been going through all types of political fire. There's so much corruption in politics that maybe God put me in that fire because he knows I can come out on the other side and make a difference. So, I don't want controversy, but I'll embrace it and walk through it.
